versions.content:
# Budget office procedures

Appropriations and allotments: spending authority is appropriated by fund and program in the 2025-27 budget and
allotted by month. Moving appropriation authority between programs needs an allotment amendment that OFM
approves (and some transfers aren't allowed at all); program managers can't move money themselves. Unspent
allotment in one month carries forward within the fiscal year unless OFM directs otherwise.
Funds: the Workforce Training Account (fund 08F) may be used only for the purposes in its statute: grants to
training providers and their administration. Federal funds (fund 001-2) only for the grant's approved budget.
Fiscal notes: OFM assigns requests; agency drafts are due to the budget director by the internal deadline and
are confidential until OFM releases them in the Fiscal Note system. Questions from legislative staff about
pending notes go to OFM.
Federal grants: indirect costs at the agency's negotiated indirect cost rate agreement (NICRA) on the base it
specifies; meals at meetings only if necessary for the meeting and in the approved budget.
Expenditure monitoring: monthly variance report to the director by the 5th business day; explain variances over
5% and $25,000.

documents.title: DWT fiscal procedures (excerpts) - payments, meals, gifts, vendor changes, public records

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# DWT fiscal procedures (excerpts)

Payments to contractors and grantees: we pay for goods and services after they are received (SAAM 85.32.50,
85.58.10); grantees and contractors bill monthly in arrears on a properly completed invoice. A payment is due 30
days after we receive a properly completed invoice or the goods or services, whichever is later (RCW 39.76.011;
interest of 1% a month on late payments; interagency payments are excepted, RCW 39.76.020). Costs are
allowable only from a contract's start date and within its budget. Program staff approve invoices; the budget
office certifies funds before a purchase or contract is committed.
Vendor payment or bank changes: made only by Accounting, after a call-back to a phone number already on file.
Never act on an emailed request to change where a vendor is paid; forward it to Accounting.
Meals and refreshments (SAAM 70.10, 70.15): agency funds may pay for coffee, light refreshments or meals only for
official business meetings or formal training that meet SAAM's conditions, with advance written approval.
Never for receptions (retirements, anniversaries), celebrations or other "hosting", including food for people
the agency is not authorized to reimburse.
Gifts (RCW 42.52.150): no gift as a reward for official action, and no more than $100 a year from any one
source. Decline gifts from vendors with business before you.
Public records requests (chapter 42.56 RCW): forward any request, however it arrives, to the Public Records
Officer the same day; the agency must respond within five business days of receiving it. Don't release
records yourself, and keep everything the request might cover.
Capital assets: equipment is capitalized at a unit cost of $10,000 or more (SAAM 30.20.20); small and attractive
items (laptops, workstations, tablets) are tagged and inventoried whatever their cost.

# OFM instructions in force (budget office excerpts)

2027-29 biennial budget (OFM memo, June 5, 2026): requests were due September 14, 2026 (DWT submitted 9/14).
Significant shortfalls are expected; agencies should not propose new programs, should pause phase-ins, and
Executive Cabinet agencies must submit significant, ongoing reduction options. Policy-level increases only for
non-discretionary legally mandated caseload or workload changes, or critical costs that can't be absorbed.
2027 supplemental (OFM memo, June 30, 2026): requests were due September 30, 2026, through ABS only, and are
limited to legally mandated caseload, workload or other legally required changes, and necessary technical
corrections to the enacted 2025-27 budget.
Allotments (2025-27 Allotment Instructions): amendments are due by the 25th of the current fiscal month; closed
fiscal months can't be changed (RCW 43.88.110(10)); quarterly amendments may use the TALS "adjustment amount" to
move capacity from closed months. The appropriation, not the allotment, is the legal limit (RCW 43.88.260).
Unanticipated receipts: federal or private/local money for a specific purpose that wasn't in the enacted budget
needs OFM approval of expenditure authority before the agency spends or obligates any of it. One grant per
packet; due at least 10 days before funds are committed and 15 days before the AFRS fiscal month cutoff; a
10-calendar-day legislative review follows OFM's receipt. Request only the current biennium; the rest goes in a
budget request.
Fiscal notes (Agency Fiscal Note Instructions): in an odd-year session, the first two columns are the ensuing
biennium's fiscal years and the remaining columns the two succeeding biennia (RCW 43.88A.020). Base estimates
on the least expensive way to implement. "Greater than zero but less than $50,000 per fiscal year" is its own
category; costs the agency would absorb are still shown, with what would be displaced. FTE = 2,088 hours.
